newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end up, but seen easing.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end up, but seen easing.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates were higher at the close on Wednesday but dealers said they expected rates to soften gradually as T$15 billion of treasury bills mature on Thursday.
The overnight interbank rate closed at 5.483 percent against Tuesday's 5.433 finish, with 30-day commercial paper at 5.50 percent against 5.20-5.25.

Money rates have been rising in the past few days as the bullish stock market has attracted huge liquidity from the banking system. Dealers expected the interbank rate to stabilise between 5.400 and 5.475 percent on Thursday.
The government bond market did not report any transaction in the afternoon after initial selling.
In late morning trade, the 10-year 84/1 yield was at 5.8400 percent, the seven-year 85/3 yield at 5.7350, the seven-year 86/3 at 5.8300 and the 10-year 86/4 at 5.9950-6.0000.
